# How decisive were these results?

Five philosophical opposites, and one of them turns out to be a trick question.


::: {.cell}

:::


**TL;DR:** a straight line's opposite is, apparently, obviously a curve, with Curve beating Point 54–8 (87%), the most lopsided call of the week by a wide margin. Fittingly, the closest race of the bunch was What's the opposite of a question?. Answer edged Statement 34–31, essentially a coin flip. Turns out the opposite of a question is itself a genuinely open question.

A quiet week on the office-alignment front: HQ and RTP picked the exact same winner on all five questions, no gap comes close to significant (all p > 0.16), and the Alignment Index for this poll alone lands at **0.63**, middle of the pack, nothing dramatic in either direction. The cumulative index holds steady at **0.83**, and the running flip tally stays put at **9**. After the last two weeks' fireworks (a record-low alignment, then a record-high one), this poll was the two offices just... agreeing.

# Do the elemental opposites travel together?

Two of these questions reach for a physical extreme rather than a strict negation: Water isn't really the *absence* of fire, and Boiling isn't the reverse of freezing so much as its temperature opposite. Let's see how much the "go with the elemental extreme" crowd overlaps.


::: {.cell}

:::


Of the 66 overlapping voters, somewhere between 18 and 41 (27%–62%) picked *both* Water and Boiling, versus about 27 (41%) expected if the two choices were unrelated. Both options were comfortable majorities on their own, so there's a solid floor under the "opposites are extremes, not negations" school of thought in this office. Melting and "no fire" just didn't have the same pull.
